tie_rule: retain every minimizing order; choose lexicographically first
search_family: all permutations of all variables, without architecture macros
predictions: Every order equals independent full assignment enumeration in each exact algebra.
For every order, work = sum_i (2*k_i+1)*product(sizes over bucket union) + 2*number(final scalar factors).
Width w gives work <= (2*m+3*n)*q^(w+1)+2*(m+n), an upper bound only.
Search evaluates exactly n! orders and charges the sum of all candidate execution counters.
Chain order (0,...,n-1) has width 1 and work (5*n-7)*q^2+3*q+2.
Star center-last has width 1 and work 3*(n-1)*q^2+(2*n-1)*q+2.
Star center-first has width n-1 and work (2*n-1)*q^n+3*sum(q^j,j=1..n-1)+2; it exceeds center-last in star4q2.
Clique orders all have width n-1 and identical structural work/memory profiles, so all n! orders tie.
Cycle5q2 has an order with width 2, without a claim that every solver must pay its dense-table upper bound.
Disconnected5q2 retains the isolated variable: its rational partition value includes a factor q; Boolean/min-plus use their own repeated-unit sum.
boundaries: Known distributive compilation, not a historically new algorithm or domain.
Search is neutral only within registered variable-order factorization; factor scopes and semiring are supplied assumptions.
Numeric bit sizes, input residence, intermediate tables, search and certificate size are reported; Python overhead and physical energy/time are not inferred.
No neural architecture, arbitrary program basis, quantum, chemical or analog physical advantage is established.
